extracted.intended_audience: members of the public and stakeholders (plan sponsors, plan fiduciaries, regulated entities, lawyers, and commenters) searching Federal Register documents about fiduciary rules
extracted.subtask_short: search results for fiduciary rule documents
extracted.subtask_description: A Federal Register search-results page listing rules, proposed rules, notices, and related documents matching the term 'fiduciary rule', including abstracts and excerpts that state regulatory standards and procedural requirements. Useful for finding rule texts, exemptions, comment deadlines, and guidance affecting ERISA fiduciaries and related entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'investment advice' fiduciary under ERISA
rubrics_metrics.description: Defines when a person renders "investment advice for a fee or other compensation, direct or indirect" with respect to plan assets such that the person is a 'fiduciary' under ERISA (applies to Title I and Title II and to IRAs).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: As stated in multiple entries: fiduciary status is determined on a transaction-by-transaction basis; one is only a fiduciary 'to the extent' the person making the recommendation meets the rule's requirements with respect to that transaction. The final/proposed rule texts and associated preambles explain scope and applicability (plans, participants, beneficiaries, and IRAs).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transaction-by-transaction test for fiduciary status
rubrics_metrics.description: Fiduciary status under the statute and proposed rules is applied 'on a transaction-by-transaction basis' — a person is a fiduciary 'to the extent' they render investment advice for a fee or other compensation with respect to that transaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limits fiduciary status to particular recommendations/transactions rather than imposing blanket fiduciary status across all activities; appears repeatedly in proposed and final Retirement Security Rule materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for relief under Prohibited Transaction Exemption (PTE) 2020-02
rubrics_metrics.description: PTE 2020-02 provides exemptive relief allowing certain compensation to investment advice fiduciaries that otherwise would be prohibited, subject to the exemption's operative terms and any amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments and republishing of operative text (noted in search results) change or clarify the conditions under which investment-advice fiduciaries may receive compensation; any reliance must comply with the exemption's explicit eligibility requirements and conditions in the operative language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary Fiduciary Correction (VFC) Program eligibility and correction requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The VFC Program permits persons to avoid potential Department of Labor civil enforcement actions and civil penalties if they voluntarily correct eligible transactions in a manner that meets the Program's requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program amendments add a self-correction feature (for certain delinquent transmittals and loan repayments), clarify eligible transactions, expand scope, and simplify administrative requirements. Eligibility for relief requires correcting transactions in the manner prescribed by the Program and meeting any specified conditions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal and co-fiduciary liability under ERISA (Sections 409 and 405)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 409 of ERISA provides that a fiduciary who breaches responsibilities shall be personally liable to make good plan losses and restore profits made through use of plan assets; Section 405 provides that a fiduciary may be liable for a co-fiduciary's breach under certain circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These statutory liability rules underpin enforcement policies (including VFC eligibility) and inform why voluntary correction programs and exemptions are structured to protect plans, participants, and beneficiaries.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fiduciary duty of prudence when selecting designated investment alternatives (safe harbor/process criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed regulation clarifies and provides a safe harbor for a fiduciary's duty of prudence in selecting designated investment alternatives (including asset allocation funds that include alternative assets).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The example process in the excerpts: the fiduciary reads and critically reviews written representations, consults a third-party investment advice fiduciary, does not know (or have reason to know) other information that would cause questioning, and after an objective, thorough, and analytical evaluation determines the product's redemption structure (or other features) is appropriate. The safe harbor is tied to conducting such a prudent, documented process.

rubrics_metrics.name: PBM (Pharmacy Benefit Manager) fee-disclosure requirement to plan fiduciaries
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed rule would require PBMs and affiliated providers of brokerage and consulting services to disclose information about their compensation to fiduciaries of self-insured group health plans subject to ERISA, so fiduciaries can assess reasonableness of contracts and compensation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disposition: disclosures are intended to enable fiduciaries to satisfy ERISA duties and to qualify for statutory prohibited transaction exemptions for service arrangements. The proposal highlights that responsible plan fiduciaries are charged with monitoring PBMs and ensuring contracts are reasonable; statutory changes may affect the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Safe-harbor and statutory equivalence for selection of annuity providers
rubrics_metrics.description: Statutory safe harbor (e.g., added by SECURE 2.0) provides a streamlined fiduciary safe harbor for selecting annuity providers for benefit distributions from individual account plans, rendering an older regulatory safe harbor unnecessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory removal of the older safe harbor is justified to avoid duplication and inadvertent traps for the unwary; the statutory safe harbor governs compliance and reduces regulatory burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards and limits for granting individual exemptions from prohibited transaction restrictions (ERISA §408(a) and PTE 84-14/QPAM rules)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department has authority under ERISA section 408(a) to grant exemptions from prohibited transaction restrictions if administrative findings are met; some class exemptions (e.g., PTE 84-14) provide narrow relief (such as limited relief for QPAMs) and individual exemptions may be conditioned.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exemptions may be conditioned on specified safeguards (e.g., independent fiduciary representation, adherence to specified procedures). The search results include examples (Northern Trust) where exemptions are conditioned in light of convictions or other facts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'significant adverse comments' in rulemaking procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: Significant adverse comments are those that oppose the rule and raise, alone or in combination, a serious enough issue related to each of the independent grounds for the rule such that a substantive response is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition determines whether a direct final rule becomes effective as published or whether the agency must withdraw or issue a new final rule responding to comments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement for FCUs to maintain written policies for eligible-obligations transactions (principles-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: Proposed NCUA change: federal credit unions must maintain written policies for purchase, sale, and pledge of eligible obligations, but prescriptive lists of required items are proposed to be removed in favor of a more principles-based approach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposal would retain the written-policy requirement while removing detailed prescriptive items and detailed requirements regarding conflicts of interest and compensation because those matters are governed elsewhere (by bylaws and fiduciary duties).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule allowing a duly appointed fiduciary to assume operation of a municipal securities dealer (Exchange Act Rule 15Ba2-5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rule 15Ba2-5 permits a duly appointed (or duly qualified) fiduciary to assume immediate responsibility for operation of a registered municipal securities dealer's business so the fiduciary need not register as a municipal securities dealer before assuming operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule implements Section 15B(a) of the Exchange Act and provides a regulatory pathway for fiduciaries stepping in to operate a dealer in receivership or similar situations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendment to PTE 2002-51 to permit excise tax relief for transactions corrected via the VFC Program
rubrics_metrics.description: PTE 2002-51 is amended to allow excise tax relief from excise taxes imposed by the Internal Revenue Code for certain eligible transactions corrected pursuant to the Department of Labor's Voluntary Fiduciary Correction Program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This amendment links tax relief under the Code to correction under the VFC Program and alters eligible corrective-relief mechanics for plans and fiduciaries seeking excise-tax relief.

rubrics_metrics.name: Independent fiduciary requirement and selection process for certain proposed exemptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Some proposed individual exemptions require that an independent fiduciary represent the plan for all purposes with respect to the transaction (e.g., sales of plan property); the selection of an independent fiduciary should be via a prudent process (e.g., RFP) and documented engagement agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The excerpts explain that applicants represent that trustees engaged in a prudent process (RFP asking for examples of similar services) and entered an engagement agreement with the independent fiduciary; this requirement is a condition of some exemptions designed to protect plan interests where conflicts might exist.
